title: Snooze! Investigating the User-Defined Deferral of Mobile Notifications

scope_decision.qualification: NHistory processes Android notification-listener observations and app interaction events. It is not a UsageStats foreground-app or app-session method; its five-second interval is a temporary UI affordance.
scope_decision.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Figure 2 and SYSTEM/NHistory/Snoozing Notifications

source_artifacts.identity_verification: PDF p. 1 prints the full title, five authors, MobileHCI '18 line, and DOI 10.1145/3229434.3229436.
source_artifacts.inspection: All thirteen pages inspected, with method and quantitative-result passages checked against layout text and Figures 1–5.
Searchable extraction; PDF page/section/figure locators, not extracted line positions, are authoritative.

source_method_variants: One NHistory collector with two genuine user-selectable snooze methods, duration and point-in-time. Initial method is randomly assigned; users may change it in settings. Each method offers eight choices at a given moment, but point-in-time choices depend on time of day.

In-app long-press/button and notification-drawer dismissal followed by a temporary snooze-action notification are two interaction entry paths. Five seconds is the latter prompt's lifetime, not an event-grouping threshold.
In-the-wild and controlled-week studies use NHistory; they are separate study populations, not two asserted collector algorithms.

analysis_outputs_and_population_warnings: Five seconds controls visibility of a follow-up UI notification only. It is not a session, response, or deduplication gap.

The 20,345,277 posted-event count includes replacement/update floods and cannot be interpreted as unique notifications; no text was collected, so the paper expressly could not remove those floods by content.
The 2,648-to-2,390 exclusion concerns installation-day snooze events; 2,390 is not the number of distinct notifications. The 1,191 initial-item set and 463 repeat-snoozed items have different units.

Figure 4's full point-in-time label list is pooled across times of day; only eight choices are presented at one time. Future group/rule/location snoozing discussed later is not an implemented study variant.

semantic_residues_vs_current_linkml.source_case: One notification item may generate multiple snooze interactions and a re-triggered notification, while posts/replacements are not unique items.
semantic_residues_vs_current_linkml.existing_terms: MethodSettingAssertion, AcquisitionProtocol, OperationDefinition and NotificationAttributionPolicy can document the source method; UsageEventRecord is UsageStats-shaped.
semantic_residues_vs_current_linkml.residue: Test a source-shaped import and reload of item identity, post/update, snooze, and re-trigger links before adding a typed assertion or adapter. Do not coerce listener callbacks into UsageStats rows.

semantic_residues_vs_current_linkml.source_case: A five-second temporary prompt, two snooze methods, and a two-day user inclusion rule have different targets and stages.
semantic_residues_vs_current_linkml.existing_terms: Source-located MethodSettingAssertion and OperationDefinition can retain the distinct roles and ordered branches.
semantic_residues_vs_current_linkml.residue: No new class justified solely by these three numeric/choice values; exact point-in-time implementation is source-undisclosed.

completion_verdict: Bounded full-text source draft for Android notification and interaction processing. It is not a canonical profile admission or proof of executable notification-instance processing; exact collector, join, scheduling, and analysis formulas remain unreleased or unspecified.
